Focus will be moved to the release history panel."> Release history Python-tesseract is an optical character recognition (OCR) tool for python. That is, it will recognize and “read” the text embedded in images. Python-tesseract is a wrapper for Google’s Tesseract-OCR Engine . It is also useful as a stand-alone invocation script to tesseract, as it can read all image types supported by the Pillow and Leptonica imaging libraries, including jpeg, png, gif, bmp, tiff, and others. Additionally, if used as a script, Python-tesseract will print the recognized text instead of writing it to a file. USAGE Quickstart Note : Test images are located in the tests/data folder of the Git repo. Library usage: from PIL import Image import pytesseract # If you don't have tesseract executable in your PATH, include the following: pytesseract . pytesseract . tesseract_cmd = r '<full_path_to_your_tesseract_executable>' # Example tesseract_cmd = r'C:\Program Files (x86)\Tesseract-OCR\tesseract' # Simple image to string print ( pytesseract . image_to_string ( Image . open ( 'test.png' ))) # In order to bypass the image conversions of pytesseract, just use relative or absolute image path # NOTE: In this case you should provide tesseract supported images or tesseract will return error print ( pytesseract . image_to_string ( 'test.png' )) # List of available languages print ( pytesseract . get_languages ( config = '' )) # French text image to string print ( pytesseract . image_to_string ( Image . open ( 'test-european.jpg' ), lang = 'fra' )) # Batch processing with a single file containing the list of multiple image file paths print ( pytesseract . image_to_string ( 'images.txt' )) # Timeout/terminate the tesseract job after a period of time try : print ( pytesseract . image_to_string ( 'test.jpg' , timeout = 2 )) # Timeout after 2 seconds print ( pytesseract . image_to_string ( 'test.jpg' , timeout = 0.5 )) # Timeout after half a second except RuntimeError as timeout_error : # Tesseract processing is terminated pass # Get bounding box estimates print ( pytesseract . image_to_boxes ( Image . open ( 'test.png' ))) # Get verbose data including boxes, confidences, line and page numbers print ( pytesseract . image_to_data ( Image . open ( 'test.png' ))) # Get information about orientation and script detection print ( pytesseract . image_to_osd ( Image . open ( 'test.png' ))) # Get a searchable PDF pdf = pytesseract . image_to_pdf_or_hocr ( 'test.png' , extension = 'pdf' ) with open ( 'test.pdf' , 'w+b' ) as f : f . write ( pdf ) # pdf type is bytes by default # Get HOCR output hocr = pytesseract . image_to_pdf_or_hocr ( 'test.png' , extension = 'hocr' ) # Get ALTO XML output xml = pytesseract . image_to_alto_xml ( 'test.png' ) # getting multiple types of output with one call to save compute time # currently supports mix and match of the following: txt, pdf, hocr, box, tsv text , boxes = pytesseract . run_and_get_multiple_output ( 'test.png' , extensions = [ 'txt' , 'box' ]) Support for OpenCV image/NumPy array objects import cv2 img_cv = cv2 . imread ( r '/<path_to_image>/digits.png' ) # By default OpenCV stores images in BGR format and since pytesseract assumes RGB format, # we need to convert from BGR to RGB format/mode: img_rgb = cv2 . cvtColor ( img_cv , cv2 . COLOR_BGR2RGB ) print ( pytesseract . image_to_string ( img_rgb )) # OR img_rgb = Image . frombytes ( 'RGB' , img_cv . shape [: 2 ], img_cv , 'raw' , 'BGR' , 0 , 0 ) print ( pytesseract . image_to_string ( img_rgb )) If you need custom configuration like oem / psm , use the config keyword. # Example of adding any additional options custom_oem_psm_config = r '--oem 3 --psm 6' pytesseract . image_to_string ( image , config = custom_oem_psm_config ) # Example of using pre-defined tesseract config file with options cfg_filename = 'words' pytesseract . run_and_get_output ( image , extension = 'txt' , config = cfg_filename ) Add the following config, if you have tessdata error like: “Error opening data file…” # Example config: r'--tessdata-dir "C:\Program Files (x86)\Tesseract-OCR\tessdata"' # It's important to add double quotes around the dir path. tessdata_dir_config = r '--tessdata-dir "<replace_with_your_tessdata_dir_path>"' pytesseract . image_to_string ( image , lang = 'chi_sim' , config = tessdata_dir_config ) Functions get_languages Returns all currently supported languages by Tesseract OCR. get_tesseract_version Returns the Tesseract version installed in the system. image_to_string Returns unmodified output as string from Tesseract OCR processing image_to_boxes Returns result containing recognized characters and their box boundaries image_to_data Returns result containing box boundaries, confidences, and other information. Requires Tesseract 3.05+. For more information, please check the Tesseract TSV documentation image_to_osd Returns result containing information about orientation and script detection. image_to_alto_xml Returns result in the form of Tesseract’s ALTO XML format. run_and_get_output Returns the raw output from Tesseract OCR. ## Implementation plan: Background ingestion pipeline

### 1. Dispatch processing after a successful upload

Update `POST /api/documents/upload` to accept FastAPI’s `BackgroundTasks`.

Flow:

1. Validate and persist the upload.
2. Insert the SQLite record as `PROCESSING`.
3. Register `DocumentIngestionService.process_document(document_id)` with `background_tasks.add_task(...)`.
4. Return the existing `202 Accepted` response.

The background task receives only the durable document UUID. It will reopen the file using the path stored in SQLite, avoiding reliance on the request-scoped `UploadFile`.

### 2. Add page-oriented text extraction

Create a dedicated text extraction service returning records such as:

```python
ExtractedPage(
    page_number=1,
    text="...",
    extraction_method="pypdf",
)
```

#### PDFs

For every page:

1. Use `pypdf.PdfReader` and `page.extract_text()`.
2. If the extracted page has insufficient usable text, render only that page to an image.
3. Run `pytesseract.image_to_string()` on the rendered page.
4. Preserve the one-based PDF page number.

`pypdf` cannot rasterize scanned PDF pages itself, so `pypdfium2` will be used only as the local PDF-to-image rendering bridge. This avoids requiring Poppler.

A configurable minimum-character threshold will detect pages that likely contain only scans or unusable extracted text. If OCR produces nothing but pypdf produced some text, the pypdf result will be retained.

#### Images

Use Pillow and Tesseract directly. Multi-frame images such as TIFF files will be processed frame-by-frame, with each frame treated as a numbered page.

If no usable text can be extracted from the entire document, processing will fail rather than creating empty vector records.

### 3. Add page-aware chunking

Create a deterministic chunking service with defaults matching the original design:

- Chunk size: 500 characters
- Overlap: 50 characters
- Never merge content across page boundaries
- Skip empty chunks

Each chunk will contain:

- Stable chunk ID
- Document UUID
- Original filename
- One-based page number
- Page-local chunk index
- Character start/end offsets
- Chunk text
- Extraction method

Example stable ID:

```text
{document_id}:p0001:c0000
```

This makes ingestion retry-safe and gives the future query endpoint traceable citations.

### 4. Generate local embeddings

Add a sentence-transformers embedding service using:

```text
sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
```

Behavior:

- CPU by default
- Lazy model initialization so API startup stays responsive
- Batch encoding
- Normalized embeddings
- No API key or external inference service
- Lock-protected model initialization/encoding for concurrent background tasks

The default model will be downloaded during the Docker image build and cached inside the image so document ingestion does not require a model download at runtime.

### 5. Persist chunks in local ChromaDB

Add a Chroma vector-store service using a local `PersistentClient` pointed at:

```text
data/chroma
```

Use a shared collection such as:

```text
document_chunks
```

For every chunk, store:

- Caller-generated sentence-transformer embedding
- Chunk text as the Chroma document
- Stable chunk ID
- Metadata:
  - `document_id`
  - `filename`
  - `page_number`
  - `chunk_index`
  - `char_start`
  - `char_end`
  - `extraction_method`

Before re-ingesting a document, delete existing records filtered by `document_id`, then upsert the new records. If ingestion fails after a partial vector write, attempt to remove that document’s vectors before recording failure.

### 6. Add SQLite status transitions

Extend `DocumentRepository` with:

```python
update_status(
    document_id,
    status,
    error_message,
    updated_at,
)
```

The SQLite implementation will update:

- `status`
- `error_message`
- `updated_at`

Pipeline transitions:

```text
PROCESSING
    ├── successful extraction/chunking/embedding/ingestion → READY
    └── any pipeline exception                            → FAILED
```

On success:

- Set `READY`
- Clear `error_message`
- Update `updated_at`

On failure:

- Log the full exception server-side
- Store a bounded, useful error message in SQLite
- Set `FAILED`
- Preserve the uploaded source file for inspection or future retry

### 7. Add configuration

Add `LOGIPRO_*` settings for:

- OCR language, default `eng`
- OCR render DPI, default approximately `200`
- OCR timeout
- Minimum extracted-text threshold
- Chunk size, default `500`
- Chunk overlap, default `50`
- Embedding model
- Embedding batch size
- Embedding device, default `cpu`
- Chroma collection name

Configuration validation will ensure overlap is smaller than chunk size.

### 8. Update container dependencies

Add Python dependencies for:

- `pypdf`
- `pypdfium2`
- `Pillow`
- `pytesseract`
- `sentence-transformers`
- `chromadb`

Update the Docker image to install:

- `tesseract-ocr`
- English Tesseract language data

No separate Chroma, embedding, OCR, queue, or worker container will be introduced.

### 9. Testing strategy

Existing upload tests currently use intentionally minimal fake PDF/image bytes. Because Starlette’s `TestClient` waits for background tasks, those tests will receive an injected recording/no-op ingestion service so they continue to test upload persistence independently.

Add focused tests for:

- Upload schedules the background task with the correct UUID.
- Digital PDF pages use pypdf text.
- Blank/scanned PDF pages trigger page-specific OCR.
- Image uploads use Tesseract.
- Multi-frame images retain frame/page numbers.
- Chunks do not cross page boundaries.
- Chunk overlap and metadata are correct.
- Embeddings and metadata are passed to Chroma.
- Successful ingestion transitions `PROCESSING → READY`.
- Extraction, embedding, or Chroma failure transitions to `FAILED`.
- Failure messages are exposed by the status endpoint.
- Existing query endpoint remains `501`.

Heavy infrastructure will be dependency-injected in unit tests to prevent model downloads and OCR variability. A small local Chroma persistence test will verify the actual storage API where feasible.

### 10. Validation

Run:

```bash
python -m compileall -q app tests
python -m pytest -q
docker compose config -q
docker compose build
docker compose up
```

Then verify an uploaded document eventually reports either:

```json
{"status": "READY", "error_message": null}
```

or:

```json
{"status": "FAILED", "error_message": "..."}
```

### Prototype limitation

FastAPI `BackgroundTasks` runs after the response in the same application process. It is suitable for this single-container prototype, but it is not a durable queue: restarting the container during processing can leave a record in `PROCESSING`. A later production version should recover stale jobs or use a durable worker queue.

Please **toggle to Act mode** to implement the pipeline.

The upload route will schedule only after durable file/SQLite creation, and the ingestion orchestrator will own all `READY`/`FAILED` transitions and cleanup.

+"""Digital text extraction with page-level Tesseract OCR fallback."""
+
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import pypdfium2 as pdfium
+import pytesseract
+from PIL import Image, ImageSequence
+from pypdf import PdfReader
+
+from app.models.ingestion import ExtractedPage
+
+
+class TextExtractionService:
+    """Extract page-aware text from supported PDF and image documents."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        ocr_language: str,
+        ocr_timeout_seconds: float,
+        pdf_dpi: int,
+        fallback_min_characters: int,
+    ) -> None:
+        self._ocr_language = ocr_language
+        self._ocr_timeout_seconds = ocr_timeout_seconds
+        self._pdf_render_scale = pdf_dpi / 72
+        self._fallback_min_characters = fallback_min_characters
+
+    def extract(self, document_path: Path) -> list[ExtractedPage]:
+        """Extract text while preserving one-based page or frame numbers."""
+        if document_path.suffix.lower() == ".pdf":
+            return self._extract_pdf(document_path)
+        return self._extract_image(document_path)
+
+    def _extract_pdf(self, document_path: Path) -> list[ExtractedPage]:
+        reader = PdfReader(str(document_path))
+        extracted_pages: list[ExtractedPage] = []
+
+        for page_index, page in enumerate(reader.pages):
+            digital_text = self._normalize_text(page.extract_text() or "")
+            if self._usable_character_count(digital_text) >= self._fallback_min_characters:
+                text = digital_text
+                method = "pypdf"
+            else:
+                ocr_text = self._normalize_text(
+                    self._ocr_pdf_page(document_path, page_index)
+                )
+                text = ocr_text or digital_text
+                method = "tesseract" if ocr_text else "pypdf"
+
+            extracted_pages.append(
+                ExtractedPage(
+                    page_number=page_index + 1,
+                    text=text,
+                    extraction_method=method,
+                )
+            )
+
+        return extracted_pages
+
+    def _extract_image(self, document_path: Path) -> list[ExtractedPage]:
+        extracted_pages: list[ExtractedPage] = []
+        with Image.open(document_path) as image:
+            for page_number, frame in enumerate(ImageSequence.Iterator(image), start=1):
+                with frame.copy() as frame_image:
+                    text = self._normalize_text(self._ocr_image(frame_image))
+                extracted_pages.append(
+                    ExtractedPage(
+                        page_number=page_number,
+                        text=text,
+                        extraction_method="tesseract",
+                    )
+                )
+        return extracted_pages
+
+    def _ocr_pdf_page(self, document_path: Path, page_index: int) -> str:
+        pdf_document = pdfium.PdfDocument(str(document_path))
+        try:
+            page = pdf_document[page_index]
+            try:
+                bitmap = page.render(scale=self._pdf_render_scale)
+                try:
+                    with bitmap.to_pil() as image:
+                        return self._ocr_image(image)
+                finally:
+                    bitmap.close()
+            finally:
+                page.close()
+        finally:
+            pdf_document.close()

+        self._batch_size = batch_size
+        self._collection: Any | None = None

+        chunks: list[TextChunk],

 31 |     def __init__(
 32 |         self,
 33 |         *,
 34 |         persist_directory: Path,
 35 |         collection_name: str,
 36 |         batch_size: int,
 37 |     ) -> None:
 38 |         self._persist_directory = persist_directory
 39 |         self._collection_name = collection_name
 40 |         self._batch_size = batch_size
 41 |         self._collection: Any | None = None
 42 |         self._lock = Lock()
 43 | 
 44 |     def replace_document(
 45 |         self,
 46 |         document_id: UUID,
 47 |         chunks: list[TextChunk],
 48 |         embeddings: list[list[float]],
 49 |     ) -> None:
 50 |         """Delete stale vectors and upsert a complete document in batches."""
 51 |         if len(chunks) != len(embeddings):
 52 |             raise ValueError("Each text chunk must have exactly one embedding.")
 53 | 
 54 |         with self._lock:
 55 |             collection = self._get_collection()
 56 |             document_filter = {"document_id": str(document_id)}
 57 |             collection.delete(where=document_filter)
 58 |             try:
 59 |                 for offset in range(0, len(chunks), self._batch_size):
 60 |                     chunk_batch = chunks[offset : offset + self._batch_size]
 61 |                     embedding_batch = embeddings[offset : offset + self._batch_size]
 62 |                     collection.upsert(
 63 |                         ids=[chunk.id for chunk in chunk_batch],
 64 |                         documents=[chunk.text for chunk in chunk_batch],
 65 |                         embeddings=embedding_batch,
 66 |                         metadatas=[self._metadata(chunk) for chunk in chunk_batch],
 67 |                     )
 68 |             except Exception:
 69 |                 collection.delete(where=document_filter)
 70 |                 raise
 71 | 
 72 |     def delete_document(self, document_id: UUID) -> None:
 73 |         """Delete vectors for one document when processing fails."""
 74 |         with self._lock:

 76 |                 where={"document_id": str(document_id)}
 77 |             )

 81 |             import chromadb
 82 |             from chromadb.config import Settings as ChromaSettings
 83 | 
 84 |             self._persist_directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
 85 |             client = chromadb.PersistentClient(

 87 |                 settings=ChromaSettings(anonymized_telemetry=False),
 88 |             )
 89 |             self._collection = client.get_or_create_collection(
 90 |                 name=self._collection_name,
 91 |                 embedding_function=None,
 92 |             )

+class DocumentIngestionService:
+    """Run extraction, chunking, embedding, and vector persistence."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        repository: DocumentRepository,
+        text_extractor: PageTextExtractor,
+        text_chunker: TextChunkingService,
+        embedding_service: EmbeddingService,
+        vector_store: VectorStore,
+    ) -> None:
+        self._repository = repository
+        self._text_extractor = text_extractor
+        self._text_chunker = text_chunker
+        self._embedding_service = embedding_service
+        self._vector_store = vector_store
+
+    def process_document(self, document_id: UUID) -> None:
+        """Process a document and record ``READY`` or ``FAILED`` in SQLite."""
+        document = self._repository.get_by_id(document_id)
+        if document is None:
+            logger.error("Cannot process missing document %s", document_id)
+            return
+        if document.status is not DocumentStatus.PROCESSING:
+            logger.info(
+                "Skipping document %s because its status is %s",
+                document_id,
+                document.status.value,
+            )
+            return
+

+            pages = self._text_extractor.extract(document.path)
+            chunks = self._text_chunker.chunk_pages(
+                document_id=document.id,
+                filename=document.filename,
+                pages=pages,
+            )
+            if not chunks:
+                raise ValueError("No usable text could be extracted from the document.")
+
+            embeddings = self._embedding_service.embed(
+                [chunk.text for chunk in chunks]
+            )

 56 |         """Process a document and record ``READY`` or ``FAILED`` in SQLite."""
 57 |         document = self._repository.get_by_id(document_id)
 58 |         if document is None:

  7 | import pypdfium2 as pdfium

 14 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

 16 | 
 17 | class TextExtractionService:
 18 |     """Extract page-aware text from supported PDF and image documents."""
 19 | 
 20 |     def __init__(
 21 |         self,
 22 |         *,
 23 |         ocr_language: str,
 24 |         ocr_timeout_seconds: float,
 25 |         pdf_dpi: int,
 26 |         fallback_min_characters: int,
 27 |     ) -> None:
 28 |         self._ocr_language = ocr_language
 29 |         self._ocr_timeout_seconds = ocr_timeout_seconds
 30 |         self._pdf_render_scale = pdf_dpi / 72
 31 |         self._fallback_min_characters = fallback_min_characters
 32 |         self._pdfium_lock = Lock()
 33 | 
 34 |     def extract(self, document_path: Path) -> list[ExtractedPage]:
 35 |         """Extract text while preserving one-based page or frame numbers."""
 36 |         if document_path.suffix.lower() == ".pdf":
 37 |             return self._extract_pdf(document_path)
 38 |         return self._extract_image(document_path)
 39 | 
 40 |     def _extract_pdf(self, document_path: Path) -> list[ExtractedPage]:
 41 |         reader = PdfReader(str(document_path))
 42 |         extracted_pages: list[ExtractedPage] = []
 43 | 
 44 |         for page_index, page in enumerate(reader.pages):
 45 |             try:
 46 |                 digital_text = self._normalize_text(page.extract_text() or "")
 47 |             except Exception:
 48 |                 logger.warning(
 49 |                     "Digital text extraction failed for page %s of %s; using OCR",
 50 |                     page_index + 1,
 51 |                     document_path,
 52 |                     exc_info=True,
 53 |                 )
 54 |                 digital_text = ""
 55 |             if self._usable_character_count(digital_text) >= self._fallback_min_characters:
 56 |                 text = digital_text
 57 |                 method = "pypdf"
 58 |             else:
 59 |                 ocr_text = self._normalize_text(
 60 |                     self._ocr_pdf_page(document_path, page_index)
 61 |                 )
 62 |                 text = ocr_text or digital_text
 63 |                 method = "tesseract" if ocr_text else "pypdf"
 64 | 
 65 |             extracted_pages.append(
 66 |                 ExtractedPage(
 67 |                     page_number=page_index + 1,
 68 |                     text=text,
 69 |                     extraction_method=method,
 70 |                 )
 71 |             )
 72 | 
 73 |         return extracted_pages
 74 | 
 75 |     def _extract_image(self, document_path: Path) -> list[ExtractedPage]:
 76 |         extracted_pages: list[ExtractedPage] = []
 77 |         with Image.open(document_path) as image:
 78 |             for page_number, frame in enumerate(ImageSequence.Iterator(image), start=1):
 79 |                 with frame.copy() as frame_image:
 80 |                     text = self._normalize_text(self._ocr_image(frame_image))
 81 |                 extracted_pages.append(
 82 |                     ExtractedPage(
 83 |                         page_number=page_number,
 84 |                         text=text,
 85 |                         extraction_method="tesseract",
 86 |                     )
 87 |                 )
 88 |         return extracted_pages
 89 | 
 90 |     def _ocr_pdf_page(self, document_path: Path, page_index: int) -> str:
 91 |         with self._pdfium_lock:
 92 |             pdf_document = pdfium.PdfDocument(str(document_path))
 93 |             try:
 94 |                 page = pdf_document[page_index]
 95 |                 try:
 96 |                     bitmap = page.render(scale=self._pdf_render_scale)
 97 |                     try:
 98 |                         with bitmap.to_pil() as image:
 99 |                             return self._ocr_image(image)
100 |                     finally:
101 |                         bitmap.close()
102 |                 finally:
103 |                     page.close()
104 |             finally:
105 |                 pdf_document.close()
106 | 
107 |     def _ocr_image(self, image: Image.Image) -> str:
108 |         return pytesseract.image_to_string(
109 |             image,
110 |             lang=self._ocr_language,
111 |             timeout=self._ocr_timeout_seconds,
112 |         )
113 | 
114 |     @staticmethod
115 |     def _normalize_text(text: str) -> str:
116 |         return (
117 |             text.replace("\x00", "")
118 |             .replace("\r\n", "\n")
119 |             .replace("\r", "\n")
120 |             .strip()
121 |         )
122 | 
123 |     @staticmethod
124 |     def _usable_character_count(text: str) -> int:
125 |         return sum(not character.isspace() for character in text)

 7 | 
 8 | class TextChunkingService:
 9 |     """Split extracted pages into overlapping chunks without crossing pages."""
10 | 
11 |     def __init__(self, *, chunk_size: int, chunk_overlap: int) -> None:
12 |         if chunk_size < 1:
13 |             raise ValueError("chunk_size must be positive")
14 |         if chunk_overlap < 0 or chunk_overlap >= chunk_size:
15 |             raise ValueError("chunk_overlap must be non-negative and smaller than chunk_size")
16 |         self._chunk_size = chunk_size
17 |         self._chunk_overlap = chunk_overlap
18 | 
19 |     def chunk_pages(
20 |         self,
21 |         *,
22 |         document_id: UUID,
23 |         filename: str,
24 |         pages: list[ExtractedPage],
25 |     ) -> list[TextChunk]:
26 |         """Return stable, page-scoped chunks and character offsets."""
27 |         chunks: list[TextChunk] = []
28 |         step = self._chunk_size - self._chunk_overlap
29 | 
30 |         for page in pages:
31 |             chunk_index = 0
32 |             for window_start in range(0, len(page.text), step):
33 |                 window_end = min(window_start + self._chunk_size, len(page.text))
34 |                 raw_chunk = page.text[window_start:window_end]
35 |                 text = raw_chunk.strip()
36 |                 if text:
37 |                     leading_whitespace = len(raw_chunk) - len(raw_chunk.lstrip())
38 |                     char_start = window_start + leading_whitespace
39 |                     chunks.append(
40 |                         TextChunk(
41 |                             id=(
42 |                                 f"{document_id}:p{page.page_number:04d}:"
43 |                                 f"c{chunk_index:04d}"
44 |                             ),
45 |                             document_id=document_id,
46 |                             filename=filename,
47 |                             page_number=page.page_number,
48 |                             chunk_index=chunk_index,
49 |                             char_start=char_start,
50 |                             char_end=char_start + len(text),
51 |                             extraction_method=page.extraction_method,
52 |                             text=text,
53 |                         )
54 |                     )
55 |                     chunk_index += 1
56 | 
57 |                 if window_end == len(page.text):
58 |                     break
59 | 
60 |         return chunks

 27 | 
 28 | class ChromaVectorStore:
 29 |     """Persist caller-generated embeddings in a local Chroma collection."""
 30 | 
 31 |     def __init__(
 32 |         self,
 33 |         *,
 34 |         persist_directory: Path,
 35 |         collection_name: str,
 36 |         batch_size: int,
 37 |     ) -> None:
 38 |         self._persist_directory = persist_directory
 39 |         self._collection_name = collection_name
 40 |         self._batch_size = batch_size
 41 |         self._client: Any | None = None
 42 |         self._collection: Any | None = None
 43 |         self._lock = Lock()
 44 | 
 45 |     def replace_document(
 46 |         self,
 47 |         document_id: UUID,
 48 |         chunks: list[TextChunk],
 49 |         embeddings: list[list[float]],
 50 |     ) -> None:
 51 |         """Delete stale vectors and upsert a complete document in batches."""
 52 |         if len(chunks) != len(embeddings):
 53 |             raise ValueError("Each text chunk must have exactly one embedding.")
 54 | 
 55 |         with self._lock:
 56 |             collection = self._get_collection()
 57 |             document_filter = {"document_id": str(document_id)}
 58 |             collection.delete(where=document_filter)
 59 |             try:
 60 |                 for offset in range(0, len(chunks), self._batch_size):
 61 |                     chunk_batch = chunks[offset : offset + self._batch_size]
 62 |                     embedding_batch = embeddings[offset : offset + self._batch_size]
 63 |                     collection.upsert(
 64 |                         ids=[chunk.id for chunk in chunk_batch],
 65 |                         documents=[chunk.text for chunk in chunk_batch],
 66 |                         embeddings=embedding_batch,
 67 |                         metadatas=[self._metadata(chunk) for chunk in chunk_batch],
 68 |                     )
 69 |             except Exception:
 70 |                 collection.delete(where=document_filter)
 71 |                 raise
 72 | 
 73 |     def delete_document(self, document_id: UUID) -> None:
 74 |         """Delete vectors for one document when processing fails."""
 75 |         with self._lock:
 76 |             self._get_collection().delete(
 77 |                 where={"document_id": str(document_id)}
 78 |             )
 79 | 
 80 |     def _get_collection(self) -> Any:
 81 |         if self._collection is None:
 82 |             import chromadb
 83 |             from chromadb.config import Settings as ChromaSettings
 84 | 
 85 |             self._persist_directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
 86 |             self._client = chromadb.PersistentClient(
 87 |                 path=str(self._persist_directory),
 88 |                 settings=ChromaSettings(anonymized_telemetry=False),
 89 |             )
 90 |             self._collection = self._client.get_or_create_collection(
 91 |                 name=self._collection_name,
 92 |                 embedding_function=None,
 93 |             )
 94 |         return self._collection
 95 | 
 96 |     @staticmethod
 97 |     def _metadata(chunk: TextChunk) -> dict[str, str | int]:
 98 |         return {
 99 |             "document_id": str(chunk.document_id),
100 |             "filename": chunk.filename,
101 |             "page_number": chunk.page_number,
102 |             "chunk_index": chunk.chunk_index,
103 |             "char_start": chunk.char_start,
104 |             "char_end": chunk.char_end,
105 |             "extraction_method": chunk.extraction_method,
106 |         }

1 | # LogiPro Document Intelligence Service
  2 | 
  3 | Local-first prototype for asynchronous extraction and natural-language querying
  4 | of shipping PDFs and images.
  5 | 
  6 | ## Implemented milestones
  7 | 
  8 | The service currently includes:
  9 | 
 10 | - A FastAPI application factory and composed routers.
 11 | - Pydantic v2 contracts for upload, status, and query workflows.
 12 | - Service-layer boundaries that keep business logic out of route handlers.
 13 | - A functional health check and OpenAPI documentation.
 14 | - Single-service Docker Compose scaffolding and persistent local data mounts.
 15 | - SQLite-backed document metadata and status lookup.
 16 | - Streamed local persistence for validated PDF and image uploads.
 17 | - FastAPI background ingestion after a successful upload.
 18 | - Per-page digital PDF extraction with Tesseract fallback for scanned pages.
 19 | - Page-aware overlapping text chunks and local sentence-transformer embeddings.
 20 | - Persistent local ChromaDB vector storage with citation-ready metadata.
 21 | 
 22 | Ollama/mock answer generation and retrieval-augmented querying are reserved for
 23 | the next milestone. The query endpoint still returns `501 Not Implemented` from
 24 | the service layer.
 25 | 
 26 | ## Upload lifecycle
 27 | 
 28 | `POST /api/documents/upload` accepts the following matching filename extensions
 29 | and media types:
 30 | 
 31 | - PDF (`.pdf`, `application/pdf`)
 32 | - JPEG (`.jpg` or `.jpeg`, `image/jpeg`)
 33 | - PNG (`.png`, `image/png`)
 34 | - TIFF (`.tif` or `.tiff`, `image/tiff`)
 35 | - BMP (`.bmp`, `image/bmp` or `image/x-ms-bmp`)
 36 | - WebP (`.webp`, `image/webp`)
 37 | 
 38 | Accepted files are saved under `data/uploads` using a generated UUID filename.
 39 | Their original safe filename, server path, `PROCESSING` status, optional error,
 40 | and UTC timestamps are recorded in `data/documents.sqlite3`. After returning
 41 | `202 Accepted`, a FastAPI background task extracts and indexes the document. The
 42 | status endpoint reads the persisted record and returns `404` for unknown IDs.
 43 | 
 44 | The processing task transitions documents as follows:
 45 | 
 46 | ```text
 47 | PROCESSING -> READY
 48 |            -> FAILED (with an error_message)
 49 | ```
 50 | 
 51 | PDF pages first use `pypdf`. Pages with little or no digital text are rendered
 52 | locally and sent to Tesseract. Images, including multi-frame TIFF files, use
 53 | Tesseract directly. Text is split into 500-character chunks with 50-character
 54 | overlap without crossing page boundaries. Chroma metadata contains the document
 55 | ID, original filename, page number, chunk index, offsets, and extraction method.
 56 | 
 57 | The default local embedding model is
 58 | `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`; the Docker build caches it in the image
 59 | so processing does not need to download a model after startup.
 60 | 
 61 | ## Run with Docker
 62 | 
 63 | ```bash
 64 | docker compose up --build
 65 | ```
 66 | 
 67 | Then visit:
 68 | 
 69 | - API metadata: <http://localhost:8000/>
 70 | - Health check: <http://localhost:8000/api/health>
 71 | - Swagger UI: <http://localhost:8000/docs>
 72 | 
 73 | Stop the application with:
 74 | 
 75 | ```bash
 76 | docker compose down
 77 | ```
 78 | 
 79 | ## Local development
 80 | 
 81 | ```bash
 82 | python -m venv .venv
 83 | # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
 84 | pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
 85 | uvicorn app.main:app --reload
 86 | pytest
 87 | ```
 88 | 
 89 | ## Project structure
 90 | 
 91 | ```text
 92 | app/
 93 |   api/            # Thin route handlers and dependency providers
 94 |   core/           # Environment-driven configuration
 95 |   models/          # Internal document domain types
 96 |   repositories/   # SQLite persistence adapters
 97 |   schemas/        # Pydantic request and response models
 98 |   services/       # Upload, extraction, chunking, embedding, vector, and RAG services
 99 | frontend/         # Simple browser UI (later milestone)
100 | data/
101 |   uploads/        # Uploaded source documents
102 |   chroma/         # Persistent ChromaDB data
103 | tests/            # API smoke and contract tests
104 | compose.yaml
105 | Dockerfile
106 | ```
107 | 
108 | ## API contracts
109 | 
110 | - `POST /api/documents/upload`
111 | - `GET /api/documents/{document_id}/status`
112 | - `POST /api/documents/{document_id}/query`
113 | 
114 | Configuration is read from environment variables prefixed with `LOGIPRO_`. For
115 | example, `LOGIPRO_DATA_DIR=/app/data` selects the container's persistent data
116 | directory.
117 | 
118 | Useful ingestion settings include:
119 | 
120 | | Variable | Default |
121 | | --- | --- |
122 | | `LOGIPRO_OCR_LANGUAGE` | `eng` |
123 | | `LOGIPRO_OCR_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | `60` |
124 | | `LOGIPRO_OCR_PDF_DPI` | `200` |
125 | | `LOGIPRO_OCR_FALLBACK_MIN_CHARACTERS` | `20` |
126 | | `LOGIPRO_TEXT_CHUNK_SIZE` | `500` |
127 | | `LOGIPRO_TEXT_CHUNK_OVERLAP` | `50` |
128 | | `LOGIPRO_EMBEDDING_MODEL` | `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2` |
129 | | `LOGIPRO_EMBEDDING_DEVICE` | `cpu` |
130 | | `LOGIPRO_EMBEDDING_BATCH_SIZE` | `32` |
131 | | `LOGIPRO_CHROMA_COLLECTION_NAME` | `logipro_document_chunks` |
132 | 
133 | > **Prototype limitation:** FastAPI background tasks execute in the API process
134 | > after the response. They are not a durable job queue. Restarting the container
135 | > during ingestion can leave a document in `PROCESSING`; a production deployment
136 | > should add stale-job recovery or a durable worker queue.

1 | """SQLite implementation of document metadata persistence."""
  2 | 
  3 | import sqlite3
  4 | from datetime import datetime
  5 | from pathlib import Path
  6 | from uuid import UUID
  7 | 
  8 | from app.models.document import DocumentRecord, DocumentStatus
  9 | 
 10 | _CREATE_DOCUMENTS_TABLE = """
 11 | CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS documents (
 12 |     id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
 13 |     filename TEXT NOT NULL,
 14 |     path TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
 15 |     status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('PROCESSING', 'READY', 'FAILED')),
 16 |     error_message TEXT,
 17 |     created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
 18 |     updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
 19 | )
 20 | """
 21 | 
 22 | 
 23 | class SQLiteDocumentRepository:
 24 |     """Store document metadata in a local SQLite database."""
 25 | 
 26 |     def __init__(self, database_path: Path) -> None:
 27 |         self._database_path = database_path
 28 | 
 29 |     def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
 30 |         connection = sqlite3.connect(self._database_path, timeout=30)
 31 |         connection.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
 32 |         connection.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
 33 |         connection.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 30000")
 34 |         return connection
 35 | 
 36 |     def initialize(self) -> None:
 37 |         """Create the database directory and documents table if needed."""
 38 |         self._database_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
 39 |         with self._connect() as connection:
 40 |             connection.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
 41 |             connection.execute(_CREATE_DOCUMENTS_TABLE)
 42 | 
 43 |     def create(self, document: DocumentRecord) -> None:
 44 |         """Insert a new document record."""
 45 |         with self._connect() as connection:
 46 |             connection.execute(
 47 |                 """
 48 |                 INSERT INTO documents (
 49 |                     id,
 50 |                     filename,
 51 |                     path,
 52 |                     status,
 53 |                     error_message,
 54 |                     created_at,
 55 |                     updated_at
 56 |                 ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
 57 |                 """,
 58 |                 (
 59 |                     str(document.id),
 60 |                     document.filename,
 61 |                     str(document.path),
 62 |                     document.status.value,
 63 |                     document.error_message,
 64 |                     document.created_at.isoformat(),
 65 |                     document.updated_at.isoformat(),
 66 |                 ),
 67 |             )
 68 | 
 69 |     def get_by_id(self, document_id: UUID) -> DocumentRecord | None:
 70 |         """Retrieve a document record by UUID."""
 71 |         with self._connect() as connection:
 72 |             row = connection.execute(
 73 |                 """
 74 |                 SELECT id, filename, path, status, error_message, created_at, updated_at
 75 |                 FROM documents
 76 |                 WHERE id = ?
 77 |                 """,
 78 |                 (str(document_id),),
 79 |             ).fetchone()
 80 | 
 81 |         if row is None:
 82 |             return None
 83 | 
 84 |         return DocumentRecord(
 85 |             id=UUID(row["id"]),
 86 |             filename=row["filename"],
 87 |             path=Path(row["path"]),
 88 |             status=DocumentStatus(row["status"]),
 89 |             error_message=row["error_message"],
 90 |             created_at=datetime.fromisoformat(row["created_at"]),
 91 |             updated_at=datetime.fromisoformat(row["updated_at"]),
 92 |         )
 93 | 
 94 |     def update_status(
 95 |         self,
 96 |         document_id: UUID,
 97 |         status: DocumentStatus,
 98 |         error_message: str | None,
 99 |         updated_at: datetime,
100 |     ) -> bool:
101 |         """Update a document's processing state and timestamp."""
102 |         with self._connect() as connection:
103 |             cursor = connection.execute(
104 |                 """
105 |                 UPDATE documents
106 |                 SET status = ?, error_message = ?, updated_at = ?
107 |                 WHERE id = ?
108 |                 """,
109 |                 (
110 |                     status.value,
111 |                     error_message,
112 |                     updated_at.isoformat(),
113 |                     str(document_id),
114 |                 ),
115 |             )
116 |             return cursor.rowcount == 1

# Sentence Transformers: Embeddings, Retrieval, and Reranking

This framework provides an easy method to compute embeddings for accessing, using, and training state-of-the-art embedding and reranker models. It can be used to compute embeddings using Sentence Transformer models ([quickstart](https://sbert.net/docs/quickstart.html#sentence-transformer)), to calculate similarity scores using Cross-Encoder (a.k.a. reranker) models ([quickstart](https://sbert.net/docs/quickstart.html#cross-encoder)), to generate sparse embeddings using Sparse Encoder models ([quickstart](https://sbert.net/docs/quickstart.html#sparse-encoder)) or to compute token-level embeddings for ColBERT-style late-interaction retrieval using Multi-Vector Encoder models ([quickstart](https://sbert.net/docs/quickstart.html#multi-vector-encoder)). This unlocks a wide range of applications, including [semantic search](https://sbert.net/examples/applications/semantic-search/README.html), [semantic textual similarity](https://sbert.net/docs/sentence_transformer/usage/semantic_textual_similarity.html), and [paraphrase mining](https://sbert.net/examples/applications/paraphrase-mining/README.html).

A wide selection of over [15,000 pre-trained Sentence Transformers models](https://huggingface.co/models?library=sentence-transformers) are available for immediate use on 🤗 Hugging Face, including many of the state-of-the-art models from the [Massive Text Embeddings Benchmark (MTEB) leaderboard](https://huggingface.co/spaces/mteb/leaderboard). Additionally, it is easy to train or finetune your own [embedding models](https://sbert.net/docs/sentence_transformer/training_overview.html), [reranker models](https://sbert.net/docs/cross_encoder/training_overview.html), [sparse encoder models](https://sbert.net/docs/sparse_encoder/training_overview.html) or [multi-vector encoder models](https://sbert.net/docs/multi_vector_encoder/training_overview.html) using Sentence Transformers, enabling you to create custom models for your specific use cases.

For the **full documentation**, see **[www.SBERT.net](https://www.sbert.net)**.

## Installation

We recommend **Python 3.10+**, **[PyTorch 2.2+](https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/)**, and **[transformers v5.0+](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers)**.

```
pip install -U sentence-transformers
```

See [Installation](https://www.sbert.net/docs/installation.html) in the docs for uv, conda, source, and editable installs, CUDA setup, and extras (`[image]`, `[audio]`, `[video]`, `[train]`, `[onnx]`, `[openvino]`, `[dev]`).

## Getting Started

See [Quickstart](https://www.sbert.net/docs/quickstart.html) in our documentation.

### Embedding Models

First download a pretrained embedding a.k.a. Sentence Transformer model.

```python
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

model = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2")
```

Then provide some texts to the model.

```python
sentences = [
    "The weather is lovely today.",
    "It's so sunny outside!",
    "He drove to the stadium.",
]
embeddings = model.encode(sentences)
print(embeddings.shape)
# => (3, 384)
```

And that's already it. We now have numpy arrays with the embeddings, one for each text. We can use these to compute similarities.

```python
similarities = model.similarity(embeddings, embeddings)
print(similarities)
# tensor([[1.0000, 0.6660, 0.1046],
#         [0.6660, 1.0000, 0.1411],
#         [0.1046, 0.1411, 1.0000]])
```

### Reranker Models

First download a pretrained reranker a.k.a. Cross Encoder model.

```python
from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder

# 1. Load a pretrained CrossEncoder model
model = CrossEncoder("cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L6-v2")
```

Then provide some texts to the model.

```python
# The texts for which to predict similarity scores
query = "How many people live in Berlin?"
passages = [
    "Berlin had a population of 3,520,031 registered inhabitants in an area of 891.82 square kilometers.",
    "Berlin has a yearly total of about 135 million day visitors, making it one of the most-visited cities in the European Union.",
    "In 2013 around 600,000 Berliners were registered in one of the more than 2,300 sport and fitness clubs.",
]

# 2a. predict scores for pairs of texts
scores = model.predict([(query, passage) for passage in passages])
print(scores)
# => [8.607139 5.506266 6.352977]
```

And we're good to go. You can also use [`model.rank`](https://sbert.net/docs/package_reference/cross_encoder/cross_encoder.html#sentence_transformers.cross_encoder.model.CrossEncoder.rank) to avoid having to perform the reranking manually:

```python
# 2b. Rank a list of passages for a query
ranks = model.rank(query, passages, return_documents=True)

print("Query:", query)
for rank in ranks:
    print(f"- #{rank['corpus_id']} ({rank['score']:.2f}): {rank['text']}")
"""
Query: How many people live in Berlin?
- #0 (8.61): Berlin had a population of 3,520,031 registered inhabitants in an area of 891.82 square kilometers.
- #2 (6.35): In 2013 around 600,000 Berliners were registered in one of the more than 2,300 sport and fitness clubs.
- #1 (5.51): Berlin has a yearly total of about 135 million day visitors, making it one of the most-visited cities in the European Union.
"""
```

### Sparse Encoder Models

First download a pretrained sparse embedding a.k.a. Sparse Encoder model.

```python

from sentence_transformers import SparseEncoder

# 1. Load a pretrained SparseEncoder model
model = SparseEncoder("naver/splade-cocondenser-ensembledistil")

# The sentences to encode
sentences = [
    "The weather is lovely today.",
    "It's so sunny outside!",
    "He drove to the stadium.",
]

# 2. Calculate sparse embeddings by calling model.encode()
embeddings = model.encode(sentences)
print(embeddings.shape)
# [3, 30522] - sparse representation with vocabulary size dimensions

# 3. Calculate the embedding similarities
similarities = model.similarity(embeddings, embeddings)
print(similarities)
# tensor([[   35.629,     9.154,     0.098],
#         [    9.154,    27.478,     0.019],
#         [    0.098,     0.019,    29.553]])

# 4. Check sparsity stats
stats = SparseEncoder.sparsity(embeddings)
print(f"Sparsity: {stats['sparsity_ratio']:.2%}")
# Sparsity: 99.84%
```

### Multi-Vector Encoder Models

First download a pretrained multi-vector a.k.a. late-interaction (ColBERT-style) model.

```python
from sentence_transformers import MultiVectorEncoder

# 1. Load a pretrained MultiVectorEncoder model
model = MultiVectorEncoder("lightonai/GTE-ModernColBERT-v1")

queries = ["What is the capital of France?"]
documents = [
    "Paris is the capital of France.",
    "Berlin is the capital of Germany.",
]

# 2. Encode queries and documents into sequences of token-level embeddings
query_embeddings = model.encode_query(queries)
document_embeddings = model.encode_document(documents)
print(query_embeddings[0].shape, document_embeddings[0].shape)
# (10, 128) (9, 128)  # one 128-dimensional vector per token

# 3. Score them with late interaction (MaxSim)
scores = model.similarity(query_embeddings, document_embeddings)
print(scores)
# tensor([[9.6037, 9.4055]])
```

## Pre-Trained Models

We provide a large list of pretrained models for more than 100 languages. Some models are general purpose models, while others produce embeddings for specific use cases.

- [Pretrained Sentence Transformer (Embedding) Models](https://sbert.net/docs/sentence_transformer/pretrained_models.html)
- [Pretrained Cross Encoder (Reranker) Models](https://sbert.net/docs/cross_encoder/pretrained_models.html)
- [Pretrained Sparse Encoder (Sparse Embeddings) Models](https://sbert.net/docs/sparse_encoder/pretrained_models.html)
- [Pretrained Multi-Vector Encoder (Late Interaction) Models](https://sbert.net/docs/multi_vector_encoder/pretrained_models.html)

## Training

> **Tip:** Using an AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, ...)? Install the [`train-sentence-transformers`](skills/) Hugging Face Agent Skill via `hf skills add train-sentence-transformers [--claude] [--global]` and ask your agent to fine-tune a model on your data.

This framework allows you to fine-tune your own sentence embedding methods, so that you get task-specific sentence embeddings. You have various options to choose from in order to get perfect sentence embeddings for your specific task.

- Embedding Models
  - [Sentence Transformer > Training Overview](https://www.sbert.net/docs/sentence_transformer/training_overview.html)
  - [Sentence Transformer > Training Examples](https://www.sbert.net/docs/sentence_transformer/training/examples.html) or [training examples on GitHub](https://github.com/huggingface/sentence-transformers/tree/main/examples/sentence_transformer/training).
- Reranker Models
  - [Cross Encoder > Training Overview](https://www.sbert.net/docs/cross_encoder/training_overview.html)
  - [Cross Encoder > Training Examples](https://www.sbert.net/docs/cross_encoder/training/examples.html) or [training examples on GitHub](https://github.com/huggingface/sentence-transformers/tree/main/examples/cross_encoder/training).
- Sparse Embedding Models
  - [Sparse Encoder > Training Overview](https://www.sbert.net/docs/sparse_encoder/training_overview.html)
  - [Sparse Encoder > Training Examples](https://www.sbert.net/docs/sparse_encoder/training/examples.html) or [training examples on GitHub](https://github.com/huggingface/sentence-transformers/tree/main/examples/sparse_encoder/training).
- Multi-Vector (Late Interaction) Models
  - [Multi-Vector Encoder > Training Overview](https://www.sbert.net/docs/multi_vector_encoder/training_overview.html)
  - [Training examples on GitHub](https://github.com/huggingface/sentence-transformers/tree/main/examples/multi_vector_encoder/training).

Some highlights across the different types of training are:

- Support of various transformer networks including BERT, RoBERTa, XLM-R, DistilBERT, Electra, BART, ...
- Multilingual and multi-task learning
- Evaluation during training to find optimal model
- [20+ loss functions](https://www.sbert.net/docs/package_reference/sentence_transformer/losses.html) for embedding models, [10+ loss functions](https://www.sbert.net/docs/package_reference/cross_encoder/losses.html) for reranker models and [10+ loss functions](https://www.sbert.net/docs/package_reference/sparse_encoder/losses.html) for sparse embedding models, allowing you to tune models specifically for semantic search, paraphrase mining, semantic similarity comparison, clustering, triplet loss, contrastive loss, etc.

## Companion Blog Posts

The following Hugging Face blog posts complement this documentation with narrative walkthroughs and full training examples:

**Training guides:**

- [Training and Finetuning Embedding Models](https://huggingface.co/blog/train-sentence-transformers): end-to-end training of bi-encoder embedding models.
- [Training and Finetuning Reranker Models](https://huggingface.co/blog/train-reranker): training Cross Encoder models for the second stage of retrieve-and-rerank pipelines.
- [Training and Finetuning Sparse Embedding Models](https://huggingface.co/blog/train-sparse-encoder): training SPLADE and other sparse encoders.

**Multimodal:**

- [Multimodal Embedding & Reranker Models](https://huggingface.co/blog/multimodal-sentence-transformers): using text, image, audio, and video models through a single API.
- [Training and Finetuning Multimodal Embedding & Reranker Models](https://huggingface.co/blog/train-multimodal-sentence-transformers): training multimodal models, with a Visual Document Retrieval walkthrough.

**Efficiency techniques:**

- [Introduction to Matryoshka Embedding Models](https://huggingface.co/blog/matryoshka): variable-size embeddings that can be truncated with minimal quality loss.
- [Train 400x faster Static Embedding Models](https://huggingface.co/blog/static-embeddings): CPU-friendly embedding models without attention.
- [Binary and Scalar Embedding Quantization for Significantly Faster & Cheaper Retrieval](https://huggingface.co/blog/embedding-quantization): post-training compression of embedding vectors.
