available * This feature is well established and works across many devices and browser versions. It’s been available across browsers since July 2015. * Some parts of this feature may have varying levels of support. See full compatibility Learn more Warning: When the code parameter is used, this method dynamically executes its value as JavaScript. APIs like this are known as injection sinks , and are potentially a vector for cross-site-scripting (XSS) attacks. You can mitigate this risk by always assigning TrustedScript objects instead of strings and enforcing trusted types . See Security considerations for more information. The setInterval() method of the Window interface repeatedly calls a function or executes a code snippet, with a fixed time delay between each call. In this article Syntax Description Examples Specifications Browser compatibility See also Syntax js setInterval(code) setInterval(code, delay) setInterval(func) setInterval(func, delay) setInterval(func, delay, param1) setInterval(func, delay, param1, param2) setInterval(func, delay, param1, param2, /* …, */ paramN) Parameters func A Function to be executed every delay milliseconds. The first execution happens after delay milliseconds. code A TrustedScript or a string of arbitrary code that is compiled and executed every delay milliseconds. This can be used instead of passing a function, but is strongly discouraged for the same reasons that make using eval() a security risk. delay Optional The delay time between executions of the specified function or code, in milliseconds. Defaults to 0 if not specified. See Delay restrictions below for details on the permitted range of delay values. param1 , …, paramN Optional Additional arguments which are passed through to the function specified by func once the timer expires. Return value A positive integer (typically within the range of 1 to 2,147,483,647) that uniquely identifies the interval timer created by the call. This identifier, often referred to as an "interval ID", can be passed to clearInterval() to stop the repeated execution of the specified function. Exceptions SyntaxError The code can't be parsed as a script. TypeError Thrown if the code parameter is set to a string when Trusted Types are enforced by a CSP and no default policy is defined. It is also thrown if the first parameter is not one of the supported types: a function, string or TrustedScript . Description The setInterval() function is commonly used to set a delay for functions that are executed again and again, such as animations. You can cancel the interval using clearInterval() . If you wish to have your function called once after the specified delay, use setTimeout() . Delay restrictions It's possible for intervals to be nested; that is, the callback for setInterval() can in turn call setInterval() to start another interval running, even though the first one is still going. To mitigate the potential impact this can have on performance, once intervals are nested beyond five levels deep, the browser will automatically enforce a 4 ms minimum value for the interval. Attempts to specify a value less than 4 ms in deeply-nested calls to setInterval() will be pinned to 4 ms. Browsers may enforce even more stringent minimum values for the interval under some circumstances, although these should not be common. Note also that the actual amount of time that elapses between calls to the callback may be longer than the given delay ; see Reasons for delays longer than specified for examples. Note: The delay argument is converted to a signed 32-bit integer, which limits the value to 2147483647 ms, or roughly 24.8 days. Interval IDs are shared with setTimeout() The method returns an identifier that uniquely identifies the interval timer created by the call. This identifier, which is often referred to as an "interval ID", can be passed to clearInterval() to stop the repeated execution of the specified function. Within the same global environment (e.g., a particular window or worker), the interval ID is ensured to remain unique and is not reused for any new interval timer as long as the original timer is still active. However, different global environments maintain their own independent pools of interval IDs. Be aware that setInterval() and setTimeout() share the same pool of IDs, and that clearInterval() and clearTimeout() can technically be used interchangeably. For clarity, however, you should try to always match them to avoid confusion when maintaining your code. Ensure that execution duration is shorter than interval frequency If there is a possibility that your logic could take longer to execute than the interval time, it is recommended that you recursively call a named function using setTimeout() . For example, if using setInterval() to poll a remote server every 5 seconds, network latency, an unresponsive server, and a host of other issues could prevent the request from completing in its allotted time. As such, you may find yourself with queued up XHR requests that won't necessarily return in order. In these cases, a recursive setTimeout() pattern is preferred: js (function loop() { setTimeout(() => { // Your logic here loop(); }, delay); })(); In the above snippet, a named function loop() is declared and is immediately executed. loop() is recursively called inside setTimeout() after the logic has completed executing. While this pattern does not guarantee execution on a fixed interval, it does guarantee that the previous interval has completed before recursing. Functions are called with the global this The functions passed to setInterval() is run with normal function call semantics for determining the reference of this . This problem is explained in detail in the JavaScript reference . For non-arrow functions, the this context is set to the globalThis (an alias for window in browsers) object. The following example demonstrates how this can cause unexpected behavior. Here, when we pass the method counter.count directly to setInterval() , the this context is lost, and the method is called on the global object instead of the Counter instance, resulting in a TypeError when the count method tries to access this : js class Counter { constructor() { this.data = new Map(); } count(item) { this.data.set(item, (this.data.get(item) || 0) + 1); } } const counter = new Counter(); counter.count("foo"); // Successfully adds "foo" to the map setInterval(counter.count, 1000, "bar"); // TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'set') To work around this, you must make sure that the function passed to setInterval has the correct this context. There are three main ways to do this: If you want to explicitly specify the this context, instead of passing the method directly, wrap the method call in another anonymous function that explicitly calls the method with the correct context: js setInterval(() => counter.count("bar"), 1000); setInterval(function () { counter.count("bar"); }, 1000); If you want to use the this context of the code that calls setInterval() , always use an arrow function, which inherits the this context of its enclosing scope: js class Counter { // … repeatedCount(item) { // BAD: the `this` context is lost in the callback setInterval(function () { this.data.set(item, (this.data.get(item) || 0) + 1); }, 1000); } } js class Counter { // … repeatedCount(item) { // GOOD: the arrow function inherits the `this` context of `repeatedCount()` setInterval(() => { this.data.set(item, (this.data.get(item) || 0) + 1); }, 1000); } } If you want to avoid extra function wrappers (which increase memory usage) while explicitly specifying the this context, you can use the Function.prototype.bind() method to create a new function with the correct this context: js setInterval(counter.count.bind(counter), 1000, "bar"); Security considerations The method can be used to execute arbitrary input passed in the code parameter. If the input is a potentially unsafe string provided by a user, this is a possible vector for Cross-site-scripting (XSS) attacks. For example, the following code shows how setInterval() might execute untrustedCode provided by a user: js const untrustedCode = "alert('Potentially evil code!');"; const id = setInterval(untrustedCode, 1000); Websites with a Content Security Policy (CSP) that specifies script-src or default-src will prevent such code running by default. You can specify unsafe-eval in your CSP to allow setInterval() to execute, but this is unsafe as it disables one of the main protections of CSP. See Inline JavaScript in the CSP guide. If you must allow the scripts to run via setInterval() you can mitigate these issues by always assigning TrustedScript objects instead of strings, and enforcing trusted types using the require-trusted-types-for CSP directive. This ensures that the input is passed through a transformation function. To allow setInterval() to run, you will additionally need to specify the trusted-types-eval keyword in your CSP script-src directive. This acts in the same way as unsafe-eval , but only allows the method to evaluate if trusted types are enabled (if you were to use unsafe-eval it would allow execution even on browsers that do not support trusted types). For example, the required CSP for your site might look like this: http Content-Security-Policy: require-trusted-types-for 'script'; script-src '' 'trusted-types-eval' The behavior of the transformation function will depend on the specific use case that requires a user-provided script. If possible you should lock the allowed scripts to exactly the code that you trust to run. If that is not possible, you might allow or block the use of certain functions within the provided string. Examples Note that these examples omit the use of trusted types for brevity. See Using TrustedScript in eval() for code showing the expected approach. Example 1: Basic syntax The following example demonstrates setInterval() 's basic syntax. js const intervalID = setInterval(myCallback, 500, "Parameter 1", "Parameter 2"); function myCallback(a, b) { // Your code here // Parameters are purely optional. console.log(a); console.log(b); } Example 2: Alternating two colors The following example calls the flashtext() function once a second until the Stop button is pressed. "stop" : "go"; } function stopTextColor() { clearInterval(intervalId); // release our intervalId from the variable intervalId = null; } document.getElementById("start").addEventListener("click", changeColor); document.getElementById("stop").addEventListener("click", stopTextColor); Result Specifications Specification HTML # dom-setinterval-dev Browser compatibility Enable JavaScript to view this browser compatibility table. **Evaluating API configurations**

I'm thinking about the origins setting and whether it could result in breaking local clients, but user mentions serving the same content. So, maybe removing it would keep things cleaner. CORS isn’t harmful, and “no CORS issues” means same origin, which might not require removal. The plan now is to simplify the CORS config for a single-origin deployment, while considering service info at `/api`. I’ll also adjust the README to reflect moving service info to `/api/info` for intuitiveness and include necessary tests.**Improving upload process**

I'm thinking about how to handle form submissions by preventing the default behavior. When using `fetch` for uploads with `FormData`, I won't explicitly set the `Content-Type`. For polling status, I can create a function to check the status at intervals without using `setInterval`, which avoids overlaps. I’ll set up an `AbortController` to manage active requests, and clear on new uploads. If the status is already ready, I'll use the initial upload response, polling until I reach a terminal state like FAILED or READY. Additionally, I might want to limit consecutive failures to five before prompting a retry.**Planning polling mechanism**

I'm considering using `setTimeout` with recursion after a catch for polling. Maybe I can implement exponential backoff, keeping it around 2 seconds for retries. The user wants to continue polling until the status is ready, but I should stop if I hit terminal failed statuses. For the UI, I'll create a two-column layout for desktop and a single column for mobile. I’ll use status colors, avoid external resources like CDN/fonts, and rely on local system fonts within a single container. Also, I’ll include a `<main>` tag, labels, and live regions, plus optional file drag-and-drop.

## Frontend implementation plan

### 1. Build a dependency-free frontend

Use plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript because no frontend framework is currently installed and the requested interface is small.

Create:

```text
frontend/
├── index.html
├── styles.css
└── app.js
```

No CDN assets, npm build, or second web server will be required.

### 2. Serve the frontend from FastAPI

Update the FastAPI application to:

- Serve `frontend/index.html` from `GET /`
- Mount frontend assets at `/assets`
- Move the existing JSON service metadata from `/` to `GET /api/info`
- Keep Swagger UI at `/docs`
- Keep all existing API endpoints under `/api`

The application will use:

- `FileResponse` for the HTML entry point
- `StaticFiles` for CSS and JavaScript

Since the UI and API share the same origin and port, all frontend requests can use relative URLs and require no CORS handling. The now-unnecessary CORS middleware and frontend-origin configuration can be removed.

### 3. Create the upload interface

The upload panel will provide:

- File input restricted to the supported PDF/image formats
- Selected filename and size
- Upload button
- Disabled/loading state while uploading
- Clear upload errors
- Status badge with these states:
  - No document
  - `PROCESSING`
  - `READY`
  - `FAILED`
- Current document filename and shortened UUID

The browser will submit a `FormData` request to:

```http

```

It will not set `Content-Type` manually, allowing the browser to generate the multipart boundary.

### 4. Poll processing status

After a successful `202` response, JavaScript will poll:

```http
GET /api/documents/{document_id}/status
```

Polling behavior:

- Immediate first status check
- Continue approximately every 1.5–2 seconds
- Stop on `READY`
- Stop and show `error_message` on `FAILED`
- Retry temporary network errors
- Cancel stale polling when a different file is uploaded
- Cancel polling when the page is unloaded

A recursive `setTimeout` flow will be used instead of `setInterval`, preventing overlapping asynchronous requests.

### 5. Lock and unlock the Q&A panel

The Q&A controls will be inside a disabled fieldset until the document reaches `READY`.

Once ready, analysts can:

- Enter a natural-language question
- Submit with the button or keyboard
- See a loading state during retrieval/generation
- Ask multiple questions without re-uploading

Requests will use:

```http
POST /api/documents/{document_id}/query
Content-Type: application/json

  "top_k": 5
}
```

A new upload will clear the previous question history and lock the Q&A panel again.

Each answer card will contain:

- The analyst’s question
- Generated answer
- Provider indicator:
  - Ollama model
  - Mock fallback
- Fallback badge when applicable
- Ordered source citations

Each citation will display:

- Page number
- Relevance score as a percentage
- Source snippet
- Chunk identifier in secondary detail

All API text will be inserted using DOM `textContent`, not `innerHTML`, preventing document text or model output from injecting markup.

The layout will use:

- A compact application header
- Upload/status card
- Q&A card
- Responsive two-column desktop layout
- Single-column mobile layout
- Neutral logistics-oriented colors
- Clear status colors
- System fonts only
- Visible keyboard focus
- Accessible labels
- `aria-live` regions for upload, status, and query updates
- Reduced-motion support

A local Content Security Policy will restrict scripts, styles, and API connections to the same origin.

Frontend JavaScript will normalize:

- JSON `{ "detail": "..." }` errors
- FastAPI validation error arrays
- Network failures
- Failed document-processing messages
- Ollama-required `503` responses
- Unexpected response bodies

Buttons and inputs will always be restored after failures so reviewers can retry.

1 | # LogiPro Document Intelligence Service
  2 | 
  3 | Local-first prototype for asynchronous extraction and natural-language querying
  4 | of shipping PDFs and images.
  5 | 
  6 | ## Implemented milestones
  7 | 
  8 | The service currently includes:
  9 | 
 10 | - A FastAPI application factory and composed routers.
 11 | - Pydantic v2 contracts for upload, status, and query workflows.
 12 | - Service-layer boundaries that keep business logic out of route handlers.
 13 | - A functional health check and OpenAPI documentation.
 14 | - Single-service Docker Compose scaffolding and persistent local data mounts.
 15 | - SQLite-backed document metadata and status lookup.
 16 | - Streamed local persistence for validated PDF and image uploads.
 17 | - FastAPI background ingestion after a successful upload.
 18 | - Per-page digital PDF extraction with Tesseract fallback for scanned pages.
 19 | - Page-aware overlapping text chunks and local sentence-transformer embeddings.
 20 | - Persistent local ChromaDB vector storage with citation-ready metadata.
 21 | - Document-scoped semantic search with page-numbered source citations.
 22 | - Optional local Ollama answers with an immediate grounded mock fallback.
 23 | 
 24 | No paid API key or hosted inference service is required.
 25 | 
 26 | The responsive browser interface is served directly by FastAPI from the same
 27 | container and origin as the API. It provides upload progress, automatic status
 28 | polling, a Q&A workspace that unlocks at `READY`, and page-numbered citations.
 29 | 
 30 | ## Upload lifecycle
 31 | 
 32 | `POST /api/documents/upload` accepts the following matching filename extensions
 33 | and media types:
 34 | 
 35 | - PDF (`.pdf`, `application/pdf`)
 36 | - JPEG (`.jpg` or `.jpeg`, `image/jpeg`)
 37 | - PNG (`.png`, `image/png`)
 38 | - TIFF (`.tif` or `.tiff`, `image/tiff`)
 39 | - BMP (`.bmp`, `image/bmp` or `image/x-ms-bmp`)
 40 | - WebP (`.webp`, `image/webp`)
 41 | 
 42 | Accepted files are saved under `data/uploads` using a generated UUID filename.
 43 | Their original safe filename, server path, `PROCESSING` status, optional error,
 44 | and UTC timestamps are recorded in `data/documents.sqlite3`. After returning
 45 | `202 Accepted`, a FastAPI background task extracts and indexes the document. The
 46 | status endpoint reads the persisted record and returns `404` for unknown IDs.
 47 | 
 48 | The processing task transitions documents as follows:
 49 | 
 50 | ```text
 51 | PROCESSING -> READY
 52 |            -> FAILED (with an error_message)
 53 | ```
 54 | 
 55 | PDF pages first use `pypdf`. Pages with little or no digital text are rendered
 56 | locally and sent to Tesseract. Images, including multi-frame TIFF files, use
 57 | Tesseract directly. Text is split into 500-character chunks with 50-character
 58 | overlap without crossing page boundaries. Chroma metadata contains the document
 59 | ID, original filename, page number, chunk index, offsets, and extraction method.
 60 | 
 61 | The default local embedding model is
 62 | `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`; the Docker build caches it in the image
 63 | so processing does not need to download a model after startup.
 64 | 
 65 | ## Ask questions
 66 | 
 67 | Only documents with status `READY` can be queried. `PROCESSING` and `FAILED`
 68 | documents return `409 Conflict`, and unknown IDs return `404 Not Found`.
 69 | 
 70 | ```bash
 71 | curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/documents/DOCUMENT_ID/query \
 72 |   -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 73 |   -d '{"question":"What is the gross shipment weight?","top_k":5}'
 74 | ```
 75 | 
 76 | The response includes the generated answer and the retrieved source chunks:
 77 | 
 78 | ```json
 79 | {
 80 |   "document_id": "...",
 81 |   "question": "What is the gross shipment weight?",
 82 |   "answer": "The gross shipment weight is 2500 kg [1].",
 83 |   "citations": [
 84 |     {
 85 |       "chunk_id": "...:p0002:c0000",
 86 |       "page_number": 2,
 87 |       "text": "Gross shipment weight: 2500 kg",
 88 |       "relevance_score": 0.91
 89 |     }
 90 |   ],
 91 |   "llm_provider": "mock",
 92 |   "used_fallback": true
 93 | }
 94 | ```
 95 | 
 96 | ### LLM modes
 97 | 
 98 | `LOGIPRO_LLM_MODE` supports:
 99 | 
100 | - `auto` (default): try Ollama, then use the grounded mock fallback if Ollama is
101 |   unavailable or returns an invalid response.
102 | - `mock`: skip Ollama and immediately return an extractive answer from the most
103 |   relevant source chunks. This is the fastest reviewer setup.
104 | - `ollama`: require Ollama and return `503 Service Unavailable` if it cannot be
105 |   reached.
106 | 
107 | To force immediate fallback mode:
108 | 
109 | ```bash
110 | LOGIPRO_LLM_MODE=mock docker compose up --build
111 | ```
112 | 
113 | To use Ollama, run it on the host and install the configured model, for example:
114 | 
115 | ```bash
116 | ollama pull llama3.2
117 | ollama serve
118 | docker compose up --build
119 | ```
120 | 
121 | Compose points the application at `http://host.docker.internal:11434`. For local
122 | Python development outside Docker, the default is `http://localhost:11434`.
123 |

128 | ```

133 | - API metadata: <http://localhost:8000/api/info>
134 | - Health check: <http://localhost:8000/api/health>

Implemented the complete same-origin frontend.

### Frontend features

- Shipping PDF and image upload
- Supported file type validation
- Selected filename and file size display
- Processing status badge:
  - No document
  - `PROCESSING`
  - `READY`
  - `FAILED`
- Automatic non-overlapping status polling
- Processing failure messages
- Q&A panel locked until the document reaches `READY`
- Multiple questions per ready document
- Answer cards showing:
  - Analyst question
  - Generated answer
  - Ollama or mock provider
  - Fallback mode indicator
  - Page number
  - Source snippet
  - Relevance percentage
  - Chunk identifier
- Responsive desktop/mobile layout
- Accessible labels, focus styles, disabled states, and live status regions
- Reduced-motion support
- Content Security Policy restricted to same-origin assets/API calls

### FastAPI integration

FastAPI now serves:

- Browser UI: `http://localhost:8000/`
- CSS and JavaScript: `/assets/...`
- API metadata: `http://localhost:8000/api/info`
- Swagger UI: `http://localhost:8000/docs`

The frontend uses relative `/api/...` URLs, so no cross-origin requests are involved. The old CORS middleware and frontend-origin configuration were removed.

### Safety and lifecycle behavior

- Status polling uses recursive `setTimeout`, preventing overlapping requests.
- Polling is cancelled when another document is uploaded or the page closes.
- Old query responses are discarded if a new document is uploaded.
- Server-provided filenames, answers, errors, and citations use `textContent`; no dynamic `innerHTML` is used.
- Controls recover correctly after upload/query failures.

### Files added

- `frontend/index.html`
- `frontend/styles.css`
- `frontend/app.js`

### Validation

- Python compilation: **passed**
- JavaScript syntax check: **passed**
- Docker Compose configuration: **passed**
- Full test suite: **45 passed in 4.36s**
- Root HTML, static CSS/JS, API metadata, upload/status/query APIs, and citation UI references are covered by tests.

## Architecture analysis & proposal

### The Problem
1. **Broken Newlines / Weird Whitespace**: PDFs extracted via `pypdf` often emit text where each word or short phrase has line breaks (e.g. `Bill\nof\nlading\nnumber\nABC123`), because PDF drawing commands position individual glyph runs with newlines in text extraction mode. Currently, `TextExtractionService._normalize_text` only replaces `\r\n` and `\r` with `\n` and strips leading/trailing whitespace. It does not reassemble broken lines into clean sentences or collapse intra-sentence newlines.
2. **Frontend `white-space: pre`**:
   In `frontend/styles.css`:
   - `.answer-text` has `white-space: pre-wrap;`
   - `.citation-snippet` has `white-space: pre-wrap;`
   When `white-space: pre-wrap` is applied, any residual single newlines preserved in the text cause words to render on separate lines in the browser.

---

### Proposed Solution

#### 1. Text Normalization Pipeline (`app/services/text_extraction_service.py`)
Enhance `_normalize_text` (or extract to a dedicated text normalizer):
- Replace null bytes (`\x00`) and normalize carriage returns (`\r\n`, `\r` -> `\n`).
- Replace horizontal tabs and non-breaking spaces with standard space (` `).
- Collapse multiple horizontal spaces/tabs into a single space (`[^\S\n]+` -> ` `).
- Normalize paragraphs vs broken single newlines:
  - If lines are separated by 2 or more newlines (`\n{2,}`), preserve paragraph separation (e.g. `\n\n`).
  - If a single newline is preceded by a hyphen at the end of a line (e.g. `trans-\nportation`), de-hyphenate to `transportation`.
  - If a line break occurs between regular words (e.g., `word\nnext`), join them with a single space `word next`.
  - Avoid collapsing across distinct paragraph or list boundaries if double-spaced.
- Strip leading and trailing whitespace from the final normalized text and each paragraph.

Also check if `TextChunkingService` needs to work on this cleaned text: since `TextExtractionService.extract()` produces `ExtractedPage.text`, normalizing at the extraction level guarantees both page text and all downstream chunks receive the cleaned, sentence-flowing text.

#### 2. Frontend CSS (`frontend/styles.css`)
In `frontend/styles.css`:
- Change `.answer-text`:
  - Replace `white-space: pre-wrap;` with standard wrapping (e.g., remove `white-space: pre-wrap;` or use `white-space: normal;`). Paragraphs generated by the LLM (separated by `\n\n`) can be rendered with clean margin spacing or normal text wrapping.
- Change `.citation-snippet`:
  - Replace `white-space: pre-wrap;` with `white-space: normal;` (and `line-height: 1.5;`) so citations wrap fluidly into readable sentences instead of jagged single-word line breaks.
- Ensure `tests/test_app.py` passes any updated asset assertions.

#### 3. Verification & Testing
- Add unit tests in `tests/test_text_extraction_service.py` specifically testing:
  - Word-per-line text: `Bill\nof\nlading\nnumber\nABC123` -> `Bill of lading number ABC123`
  - Hyphenated line breaks: `inter-\nnational freight` -> `international freight`
  - Multiple paragraph preservation: `Paragraph 1.\n\nParagraph 2.` -> `Paragraph 1.\n\nParagraph 2.`
  - Multiple horizontal spaces collapsed into single space.
- Verify `tests/test_app.py` asserts that `.answer-text` and `.citation-snippet` do not use `white-space: pre` or `white-space: pre-wrap`.
- Run all pytest test suites to ensure 100% pass rate.

## Plan: Configurable Ollama Model in the UI & Query Request

### Architecture & Requirements Summary
The user requested:
1. Make the Ollama model configurable directly in the UI.
2. Add an input field in the frontend for the model name (defaulting to `llama3.2`).
3. Pass this model name in the query request so that whatever model the user types in the UI is used by Ollama.
4. Ensure the LLM model field is editable if Ollama is running (or disabled/indicated appropriately if not running or in mock mode, while being enabled and editable by default when Ollama is available).

---

### Step 1: Pydantic Schema Updates (`app/schemas/query.py`)
- In `QueryRequest`:
  - Add `model: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=100)` (or `default="llama3.2"`).
  - Note: `QueryRequest` has `model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", str_strip_whitespace=True)`, so adding `model: str | None = None` formally allows this field in the JSON request payload without 422 errors.

### Step 2: Service Layer (`app/services/answer_generation_service.py` & `app/services/rag_service.py`)
- In `AnswerGenerator` protocol:
  - Update `generate`:
    ```python
    def generate(
        self,
        *,
        question: str,
        chunks: list[RetrievedChunk],
        model: str | None = None,
    ) -> GeneratedAnswer: ...
    ```
- In `OllamaAnswerGenerator`:
  - Allow `model: str | None = None` parameter in `generate()` and `_generate_with_ollama()`.
  - Use `effective_model = model or self._model`.
  - In `_generate_with_ollama`: use `effective_model` in the payload `{"model": effective_model, ...}` and return `GeneratedAnswer(..., provider=f"ollama:{effective_model}")`.
  - Add an availability check method `is_available() -> bool` on `OllamaAnswerGenerator` (pinging Ollama's base URL / version endpoint with a short timeout, e.g. 0.5s) so the API can report whether Ollama is active.
- In `RagService`:
  - Pass `request.model` to `self._answer_generator.generate(question=request.question, chunks=chunks, model=request.model)`.

### Step 3: Backend Endpoint for Ollama / LLM Status (`app/api/routes/health.py` & schemas)
- Expose an endpoint `GET /api/llm/status` (or include in `/api/info` / `/api/health`):
  - Returns `{ "ollama_available": bool, "default_model": str, "mode": str }`.
  - Check `answer_generator.is_available()`.
  - This allows the frontend to probe on load whether Ollama is running and enable/style the model input field accordingly.

### Step 4: Frontend HTML, CSS, and JS (`frontend/`)
- **HTML (`frontend/index.html`)**:
  - In the QA section (`#qa-card` inside or alongside the question form):
    - Add a form group for the Model Name:
      - `<label for="llm-model">Ollama Model</label>`
      - `<input type="text" id="llm-model" name="model" value="llama3.2" placeholder="e.g. llama3.2, mistral, qwen2.5">`
      - An accompanying status badge or helper text (e.g. `Ollama detected` or `Ollama not detected (mock fallback)`).
- **CSS (`frontend/styles.css`)**:
  - Add styles for `#llm-model` (similar input styling to `textarea`, standard height, clear focus ring).
  - Add styling for the model field container and helper text.
- **JavaScript (`frontend/app.js`)**:
  - On page load, fetch `/api/llm/status`.
  - If Ollama is running (`ollama_available === true`):
    - Set the model input to active/editable, with a green indicator or helper badge.
  - If Ollama is not running:
    - Set input disabled or show helper note that Ollama is offline and mock mode will be used.
  - When submitting `#question-form` in `askQuestion`:
    - Read `elements.modelInput.value.trim()`.
    - Include `model` in the `POST /api/documents/{id}/query` body:
      `JSON.stringify({ question, top_k: TOP_K, model: selectedModel || undefined })`.

### Step 5: Tests & Verification
- Unit test in `tests/test_answer_generation_service.py`:
  - Test custom model passed to `generate(model="custom-model")` overrides the default `test-model` in the request payload and provider string.
- Unit test in `tests/test_rag_service.py`:
  - Test `QueryRequest(question="...", model="custom-llama")` forwards the model parameter to the answer generator.
- Integration tests in `tests/test_app.py`:
  - Test `/api/llm/status` returns expected structure.
  - Test `POST /api/documents/{id}/query` accepts `model` in request body without 422 validation errors.
  - Test frontend HTML contains `#llm-model` input element.
- Run `pytest` to ensure all tests pass.

---
Please toggle to **Act mode** to execute this plan.

I have implemented configurable Ollama models in both the backend and frontend.

### Summary of Changes:

1. **API Contracts (`app/schemas/query.py`)**:
   - Added `model: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=100)` to `QueryRequest` so clients can optionally specify the target Ollama model for question answering.

2. **Runtime Status & Probe (`app/schemas/common.py`, `app/api/routes/health.py`, `app/services/answer_generation_service.py`)**:
   - Added `LlmStatusResponse` schema.
   - Added `GET /api/llm/status` endpoint to report whether Ollama is actively reachable, the default model, and the running mode.
   - Added `is_available()` method to `OllamaAnswerGenerator` that checks connectivity against Ollama's endpoint (`/api/tags`) with a short timeout.

3. **Service Layer (`app/services/rag_service.py` & `app/services/answer_generation_service.py`)**:
   - Updated `AnswerGenerator.generate()` protocol and `OllamaAnswerGenerator.generate()` to accept an optional `model` override.
   - When provided, `OllamaAnswerGenerator` uses the custom model in the Ollama `/api/chat` request payload and labels the response provider accordingly (e.g. `ollama:mistral:7b`). If omitted, it falls back to the configured default (`llama3.2`).
   - `RagService.query_document()` forwards `request.model` directly to the answer generator.

4. **Frontend UI (`frontend/index.html`, `frontend/styles.css`, `frontend/app.js`)**:
   - **HTML**: Added an "Ollama model" input field (`#llm-model`) inside the Q&A form with an active status badge (`#ollama-status-badge`) and explanatory help text.
   - **CSS**: Styled `#llm-model` and status indicators (`.ollama-online`, `.ollama-offline`, `.ollama-checking`) with clean layout, border accents, and accessibility states.
   - **JavaScript**:
     - On page load, `initLlmStatus()` queries `/api/llm/status`.
     - If Ollama is active, the status pill shows "Ollama active" and the model input is enabled/editable when the Q&A panel is unlocked, allowing users to type any local model (e.g., `llama3.2`, `mistral`, `qwen2.5`).
     - If Ollama is not active or in mock mode, the status badge reflects "Offline (Mock)" and the input is disabled with clear feedback.
     - Form submissions include `model: elements.modelInput.value.trim() || undefined` in the `POST /api/documents/{id}/query` JSON request.

5. **Testing**:
   - Added unit tests in `tests/test_answer_generation_service.py` verifying custom model overrides and availability pings.
   - Added unit test in `tests/test_rag_service.py` ensuring `QueryRequest.model` is forwarded to the generator.
   - Added integration tests in `tests/test_app.py` for `/api/llm/status` and `POST /api/documents/{id}/query` with a custom model.
   - Ran pytest: all **51 tests passed** with zero failures.

## Proposed Plan: Move LLM Configuration to Nav Bar ### 1. Goal Move the Ollama model configuration field from the Q&A form card (`#question-form`) into the right side of the top navigation bar (`.app-header .header-inner`). - The model input (`#llm-model`) should be directly accessible on the right of the header bar. - If Ollama is detected/running, the input is enabled and editable (with default `llama3.2`). - If Ollama is offline or in mock mode, it indicates offline/fallback and is disabled. - The value entered by the user in this nav bar field will continue to be passed in query requests (`POST /api/documents/{id}/query`). --- ### 2. File Changes #### A. HTML (`frontend/index.html`) - In `
`: - Update `.header-inner`: - Keep `.brand` on the left. - Inside `
` on the right side: - Add the compact LLM config widget: ```html
Detecting…
``` - Retain `API docs` and `Local-first`. - In `
` / `#question-form`: - Remove `.model-select-group` (which was inside the card). The question form now directly presents the question prompt. #### B. I have moved the LLM model configuration to the right side of the top navigation bar.

### Summary of Changes:

1. **HTML Layout (`frontend/index.html`)**:
   - Relocated the model configuration widget from the Q&A card into the header navigation bar (`.header-links`).
   - Placed `.nav-llm-group` containing:
     - Label: `Model`
     - Text input: `#llm-model` (default value `"llama3.2"`, with title and placeholder)
     - Compact status badge: `#ollama-status-badge` (`"Detecting…"`, `"Active"`, or `"Offline (Mock)"`).
   - Cleaned up `#question-form` so the Q&A panel is focused exclusively on the question prompt and action buttons.

2. **Styling (`frontend/styles.css`)**:
   - Styled `.nav-llm-group` as a pill container with subtle background and border inside the navbar.
   - Formatted the model input to a compact 130px width (scales down to 95px on narrow mobile viewports) with custom focus rings and disabled styling.
   - Removed obsolete in-card `.model-select-group` and `.model-label-row` rules.

3. **Frontend Logic (`frontend/app.js`)**:
   - The model field in the navbar is enabled whenever Ollama is detected as running, regardless of whether a document is currently uploading or ready, allowing the user to configure the model in advance.
   - When Ollama is offline or mock mode is active, the navbar input is disabled and the status badge indicates `"Offline (Mock)"`.
   - On question submission, `askQuestion` reads the current value from `#llm-model` and passes `model` in the `POST /api/documents/{id}/query` request payload.

4. **Testing**:
   - Verified that root HTML serving and asset tests in `tests/test_app.py` check for `#llm-model` and the expected JavaScript bindings.
   - Ran pytest: all **51 tests passed in 9.50s**.
